content: Clarithromycin can be administered in various forms and dosages depending on the condition being treated. Below are detailed instructions for its administration: Adult Dosage Instructions 1. General Administration Guidelines: BIAXIN Filmtab (clarithromycin tablets, USP) and BIAXIN Granules (clarithromycin for oral suspension, USP) can be taken with or without food. BIAXIN XL Filmtab (clarithromycin extended-release tablets) must be taken with food. BIAXIN XL tablets should be swallowed whole and must not be chewed, broken, or crushed. 2. Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (caused by Streptococcus pyogenes): Administer 250 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 10 days. 3. Acute Maxillary Sinusitis (caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and/or Streptococcus pneumoniae): Administer 500 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 14 days. Alternatively, administer 2 x 500 mg BIAXIN XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 14 days. 4. Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Bronchitis: For infections caused by H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, and/or S. pneumoniae: Administer 500 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7–14 days. Alternatively, administer 2 x 500 mg BIAXIN XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For infections caused by Haemophilus parainfluenzae: Administer 500 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7 days. Alternatively, administer 2 x 500 mg BIAXIN XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. 5. Community-Acquired Pneumonia: For infections caused by H. influenzae: Administer 250 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7 days. Alternatively, administer 2 x 500 mg BIAXIN XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For infections caused by H. parainfluenzae and/or M. catarrhalis: Administer 2 x 500 mg BIAXIN XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For infections caused by S. pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, and/or Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Administer 250 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7–14 days. Alternatively, administer 2 x 500 mg BIAXIN XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. 6. Uncomplicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections (caused by Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes): Administer 250 mg of BIAXIN tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7 days. H. pylori Eradication to Reduce the Risk of Duodenal Ulcer Recurrence 1. Clarithromycin/Lansoprazole/Amoxicillin: Administer 500 mg of clarithromycin, 30 mg of lansoprazole, and 1 gram of amoxicillin, all given twice daily (q12h) for 10 or 14 days. 2. Clarithromycin/Omeprazole/Amoxicillin: Administer 500 mg of clarithromycin, 20 mg of omeprazole, and 1 gram of amoxicillin, all given twice daily (q12h) for 10 days. If an ulcer is present at the start of therapy, continue omeprazole 20 mg once daily for an additional 18 days to promote ulcer healing and symptom relief. 3. Clarithromycin/Omeprazole: Administer 500 mg of clarithromycin three times daily (q8h) and 40 mg of omeprazole once daily (qAM) for 14 days. Continue omeprazole 20 mg once daily for an additional 14 days for ulcer healing and symptom relief. 4. Clarithromycin/Ranitidine Bismuth Citrate: Administer 500 mg of clarithromycin twice daily (q12h) or three times daily (q8h) and 400 mg of ranitidine bismuth citrate twice daily (q12h) for 14 days. Continue ranitidine bismuth citrate 400 mg twice daily for an additional 14 days for ulcer healing and symptom relief. This combination therapy is not recommended for patients with creatinine clearance less than 25 mL/min. Pediatric Dosage Instructions 1. General Guidelines: The usual recommended daily dose is 15 mg/kg/day, divided into two doses (q12h) for 10 days. No dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment if renal function is normal. For severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min), the dose should be halved, or the dosing interval should be doubled. Mycobacterial Infections 1. Prophylaxis: For adults, administer 500 mg of clarithromycin twice daily (b.i.d.). For children, administer 7.5 mg/kg twice daily (b.i.d.), up to a maximum of 500 mg twice daily. Note: No specific studies have been conducted for prophylaxis in pediatric populations; the recommended doses are based on treatment studies. 2. Treatment: Clarithromycin is the primary agent for treating disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) infections. It should be used in combination with other antimycobacterial drugs that demonstrate in vitro activity or clinical benefit against MAC. For adults, administer 500 mg of clarithromycin twice daily (b.i.d.). For children, administer 7.5 mg/kg twice daily (b.i.d.), up to a maximum of 500 mg twice daily. Therapy should be continued for life if clinical and microbiological improvements are observed. Constituting Instructions for Oral Suspension 1. Add half the required volume of water to the bottle and shake vigorously. 2. Add the remaining water and shake again. 3. Shake well before each use. 4. Store the constituted suspension at room temperature (15° to 30°C or 59° to 86°F) and use within 14 days. 5. Keep the bottle tightly closed and do not refrigerate.
